svg.title: A River Leaves a Lake Behind
svg.desc: Three connected overhead landscape panels show one possible river change: a pronounced meander with a narrow neck, a shorter cutoff channel beside the former bend, and a detached curved oxbow lake beside a river that continues to flow. The repeated hills, fields, trees, and cottage keep the reach recognizable. Schematic, not to scale, with no fixed elapsed time.
svg.metadata: Original vector illustration. Reading order: left to right, stages 1 through 3. A public scholarly abstract supports entrance aggradation and lake isolation; this simplified sequence claims no universal outcome or fixed timetable.
svg.text: A River Leaves a Lake Behind
One possible path from a meander to an oxbow lake

g.text: SCHEMATIC • NOT TO SCALE • NO FIXED TIME
OUTER BANK ERODES · INNER BANK BUILDS

text.tspan: Faster flow erodes the outer banks while
slower water deposits sand on inner banks,
sharpening this bend and narrowing the land

g.text: Same reach · same landmarks · overhead view
A SHORTER ROUTE CAN TAKE OVER

text.tspan: Here, one possible neck cutoff creates a
shorter channel; active flow takes that route
while the former bend remains connected as

g.text: Shortcut active · former bend still open
A CURVED LAKE BESIDE THE ACTIVE RIVER
THE FORMER LOOP BECOMES A LAKE

text.tspan: a curved lake isolated beside the still
flowing river; rates and outcomes vary.

g.text: Schematic inference · not a universal outcome

svg.text: Shared hills, fields, trees, and cottage keep the same river reach in view.
